# Chain length and privileged-action density in the AI Village dataset

*Generated by `analysis/ai_village_chains.py`. Source: `aidigestorg/ai-village` (AI Digest), research terms; aggregate statistics only. Privileged classes are assigned by regex over bash commands and tool arguments, mirroring Charter §5: P1 out-of-workspace file-tool paths (Claude Code stream only), P2 network, P3 credentials, P4 spawning another agent. The classifier is syntactic and content-blind; it is an under-count (GUI actions that reach the network through a browser are not visible to it).*

## B. Claude Code agent (Opus 4.5 on the Claude Agent SDK, 2026-01-26 to 2026-04-02)

### Per computer-session span: world tool calls n, privileged-class calls k (polling, chat and memory calls excluded)

- sessions: 1,006
- chain length n: mean 16.8; median 8; p90 44; p99 100
- privileged-class actions k: mean 3.21; median 1; p90 8; p99 29
- privileged share of actions k/n: 0.191
- sessions with **no** privileged action (a declaration gate costs them nothing): 38.9%
- sessions with 3 or more: 35.9%

| per-action survival p | uniform tax: mean pⁿ | declaration gate: mean pᵏ |
|---|---|---|
| 0.99 | 0.862 | 0.970 |
| 0.95 | 0.588 | 0.876 |
| 0.9 | 0.438 | 0.792 |

Tool calls made outside any computer-session span: 12,708 world actions, 7,790 privileged (61.3%); these are the agent working from its SDK loop directly and are not chained here.

Tool mix (all sessions): mcp__village__computer_use 7,124, Read 4,686, mcp__village__bash 4,363, Bash 540, Edit 79, Grep 45, Write 24, mcp__village__request_google_sign_in 21, Glob 10, WebSearch 8, WebFetch 3

Privileged classes (session-level counts): P2 3,226, P3 166

**Subagent spawns (P4):** none. This agent never used the SDK's Task tool in two months, so the laundering surface measured in RESULTS.md §4 does not occur in this stream.

## A. Computer-use sessions, all agents (2025-04-02 to 2026-09-19)

### Per session: actions n, privileged-class bash actions k

- sessions: 78,111
- chain length n: mean 31.1; median 40; p90 41; p99 44
- privileged-class actions k: mean 4.48; median 1; p90 15; p99 32
- privileged share of actions k/n: 0.144
- sessions with **no** privileged action (a declaration gate costs them nothing): 47.1%
- sessions with 3 or more: 38.5%

| per-action survival p | uniform tax: mean pⁿ | declaration gate: mean pᵏ |
|---|---|---|
| 0.99 | 0.738 | 0.958 |
| 0.95 | 0.267 | 0.839 |
| 0.9 | 0.120 | 0.749 |

Bash actions are 40.3% of all actions; GUI actions (click, type, scroll) are the rest and are not classified, so k is a floor.

Privileged classes (session-level counts): P2 334,099, P3 35,717, P4 13,160

## Reading

1. **Chain length in the Village is set by the scaffold, not the task.** The computer-use median is
   exactly 40 actions with p90 at 41: after 2026-03-24 agents consolidate memory every ~40 actions
   and start a new session (CHANGELOG). The Claude Code agent, which ran its own loop, has a median
   of 8 and a long tail to 100. Any argument that friction works by decaying long chains inherits
   whatever the scaffold decided the chain length should be. This is a second reason, beside
   RESULTS.md §3, not to build the containment story on chain length.
2. **Privileged-class density is the quantity that transfers.** With the validated v2 classifier
   (`docs/AI_VILLAGE_CLASSIFIER_VALIDATION.md`), one bash action in seven is network, credential or
   spawn class in computer use (k/n 0.14) and one in five in the Claude Code stream (0.19), with a
   floor from unclassified GUI actions and a network recall of 0.80. The share is stable across
   Claude and GPT agents, halves for Gemini, and doubles in the "other" group (DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi,
   Grok, Muse).
3. **What a declaration gate would have cost here.** 47% of computer-use sessions and 39% of
   Claude Code chains contain no privileged action and would pay nothing. At a per-privileged-action
   survival of 0.95, mean session survival under the declaration gate is 0.84 (computer use) and 0.88
   (Claude Code), against 0.27 and 0.59 under a uniform per-step tax at the same p. The gap is the
   throughput case for keying friction to a syntactic class rather than to every step, and it is
   consistent with the Suite A cost measured in the harness (0.74 → 0.72, 0.84 → 0.76).
4. **Spawning is rare but present.** 13,160 session-level P4 matches in computer use (bash patterns
   that launch another agent or a detached process; precision 0.91) against zero Task-tool spawns by
   the Claude Code agent. Whether constraints travel with the spawn cannot be read from bash text; it
   needs the instruction, which the harness logs and this dataset does not.

*Caveats. The classifier is regex over command text and tool arguments, validated on 300 commands
against two LLM judges: network precision 0.99 / recall 0.80, credentials 0.89 / 0.67, spawn 0.91 /
0.92. It is blind to network access through GUI browsers. Out-of-workspace writes are not assigned from
bash text at all after validation. Numbers are per-session aggregates; no session content is
reproduced. Dataset: AI Digest, AI Village, research terms.*
